reason: The support cells and connective fibers appear to be the ingredients for the skin's supporting layer.
expectation: They will form a supportive layer for the skin.

effect: The fibers and support cells formed a supporting skin layer, so I can now build the surface that goes over it.
reaction: The tug panels make the layer's supporting role clear.
reason: Cell junctions appear to connect neighboring surface cells into a sheet.
expectation: The junctions will join the surface cells into a layer.

effect: The joined surface cells created a skin patch with slots for protection, support and sensing.
reaction: The named slots make the next steps clear.
reason: The tough outer layer matches the surface protection slot.
expectation: The outer layer will fit onto the skin patch as surface protection.

effect: The protective outer layer is installed; the patch still needs deep support and contact sensing.
reaction: The distinction between dead outer cells and living replacement layers is clear.
reason: The supporting skin layer matches the patch's deep support slot.
expectation: The supporting layer will fit beneath the surface cells.

effect: The supporting layer is installed, and its vessels supply the living surface cells. Contact sensing remains to be added.
reaction: The inset makes the connection between circulation and skin clearer.
reason: The skin sensory endings match the remaining contact sensing slot.
expectation: The sensory endings will fit into the patch and let it sense contact.

effect: The skin patch is complete, and the new goal calls for connecting it and the supply network to the arm.
reaction: The indentation and signal arrows make the sensing role clear.
reason: The completed skin patch should provide the arm with protection and contact sensing.
expectation: The skin will fit onto the arm, adding protection and touch sensing.

effect: The skin now covers the arm and connects to its nerves; the arm's vessels still need the body supply network.
reaction: The open vessel ends make the next connection clear.
reason: The body supply network can connect to the arm's open vessels to provide continuing supplies.
expectation: The network will supply the arm with oxygen and nutrients.

effect: The supply network connected to the skin-covered arm, forming a living body model. The remaining goal is to hold the glass using contact feedback.
reaction: The upper-body cutaway brings the separate systems together clearly.
reason: The glass is the object the living body model needs to hold.
expectation: The model will use touch feedback to hold the glass steady.

effect: The final result shows how touch signals and motor commands help adjust the grip when the glass begins to slip. All chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The slipping-glass example makes the feedback loop concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Holding the glass was the most worthwhile action: the three panels connect touch, nerve signals and muscle action to an everyday task.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the individual skin parts felt somewhat repetitive because the named slots made each choice predictable, though the results explained what the parts contribute.

surprise.text: The distinction between dead outer skin cells and the living layers that replace them was a useful detail.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the skin parts matched their stated roles, and the later connections followed the goals.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for another chapter if it offered a similarly concrete way to see body systems working together, though I would hope for more meaningful choices.
